# Journal — job S1 (site, 11 pages)

## 14:47 Setup
- `npm create vite@latest app -- --template vue-ts --no-interactive`, then installed the three tarballs + `vue-router` as `file:` deps.
- **low** — `@aziontech/webkit@5.12.0` declares `"@aziontech/theme": "^4.0.0"` while the shipped theme tarball is `5.2.2`; npm installs a second, nested `@aziontech/theme@4.3.1` from the registry under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/node_modules`. Two theme versions in one tree; unclear which one webkit's own source resolves at build. Nothing in README mentions the mismatch.
- `npx @aziontech/webkit init --dry-run` then `init --yes`: worked well. Clear plan output, wrote `src/webkit.css`, `postcss.config.mjs`, eslint/stylelint config, husky, `.claude/` bundle, patched `src/main.ts`. `doctor` then reports 0 fail.
- **low** — `init` adds 8 devDependencies pinned as `"latest"`, and `doctor` immediately warns about exactly that ("consider pinning"). The tool should pin what it writes.
- **low** — `init` adds a husky pre-commit hook that runs `eslint .` + stylelint on every commit; fine, but it makes the brief's checkpoint commits fail on any lint error. Decision: keep it, fix lint as I go (use `--no-verify` only if a lint rule is wrong, and journal it).
- **medium** — The note "the design system defaults to LIGHT. For dark mode set `<html data-theme="dark">`" is only printed by `init`; README "Add the theme CSS" step doesn't say how to force dark. Decision: `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in `index.html` (site is dark only).

## 14:50 Scope change
- Orchestrator reduced scope to 4 pages: site-home, site-pricing, site-contact, site-solution-web-apps. Other pages not built.

## 14:48 Finding the marketing building blocks (largest share of reading time)
- **worked well** — `llms/llms.txt` "Components: Marketing sections" is the real map: nearly every band of azion.com exists as a section (`HeroBand`, `PlatformDirectory`, `NetworkSection`, `FeatureTiles`, `MediaSplitStack`, `RecognitionMarquee`, `ClientMosaic`, `ClosingCallToAction`, `SiteNav`, `SiteFooter`…). And `examples/<name>/site-*.vue` carry real azion.com data, which made the home page mostly data entry.
- **medium** — `catalog/components/*.json` (the files README points to for "the catalog") carry no category/surface; `catalog.json` has no component list beyond `imports`. You only learn which components are "sections" from `llms.txt` headings or `llms/components/<n>.json` `category`. `rules/webkit-sections.md` tells you to use the MCP `list_components` with category `sections` — no CLI equivalent was obvious (did not try `search` for every band).
- **medium** — `llms/components/<n>.json` `props[].description` is empty for every prop I opened (site-nav, site-footer, hero-band); the descriptions only exist in the `.md` table. Types like `SiteNavMenu[]`, `HeroBandAction` are named but never defined anywhere I could read; the `.md` says "API as JSON: …/.specs/site-nav.json" — a GitHub link into `.specs/`, which README says consumers must not use.
- **low** — `llms/components/site-nav.json` lists `examples: []` though `examples/site-nav/site-default.vue` exists.
- **high** — Every marketing example uses image URLs like `'/marketing-components/logos/dafiti-extended-mono.svg'` that do not exist in a consumer app. The working form is `import x from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>'`; I found the mapping only in `src/assets/site-assets.json` and `package.json` exports (and in `docs/reviews/…/JOURNAL-B.md`, a previous review that already reported it). Some props take "registry names" instead (`HeroBand carouselMarks: 'global-fashion-group'`, `MediaSplitStack illustration: 'ai-applications'`) — two asset conventions side by side, and the registry names are listed nowhere in the docs (I read them from `src/assets/illustrations/` filenames).

## 14:52 Setup friction (several build/lint round-trips)
- **high** — `npm run build` (Vite's default `vue-tsc -b && vite build`) fails with `TS2307 Cannot find module '@aziontech/webkit/site-nav'` (also `site-footer`, `link`, `webkit-provider`), while `npx vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` resolves the same imports with zero errors. WebKit exports raw `.vue` files; build mode (`-b`) apparently resolves them inconsistently. Decision: build script = `vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && vite build`. README "Requirements → TypeScript" only mentions `htmlAttributes`; added that + `skipLibCheck`.
- **low** — `import '@aziontech/icons'` fails type-check under TS 6 (`TS2882` side-effect import without types). Added `src/env.d.ts` `declare module '@aziontech/icons'`.
- **medium** — The init-wired pre-commit hook runs `npx eslint .` and `npx stylelint "**/*.{css,scss,vue}"`, but the generated `eslint.config.mjs` has no `ignores` and there is no `.stylelintignore`, so after the first `npm run build` both lint `dist/` (hundreds of errors from WebKit's own compiled CSS/JS: hex colours, `0px`, literal ms). Added `{ ignores: ['dist/**'] }` and `.stylelintignore`. Also Vite's template comment in `vite.config.ts` fails `webkit/authoring-standards` (prose comment) — deleted it.
- Decision: one commit for setup + home (setup alone did not lint until these fixes).

## 14:53 site-home — built
- `SitePage.vue` = `SiteNav` + `<main>` + `SiteFooter` (nav/footer data copied from `examples/site-nav|site-footer/site-default.vue`, footer columns rewritten to the reference: Company/Resources/Getting Started/Developer).
- Bands: `HeroBand kind="centered"` (highlight + title, client ticker via `carouselMarks`), `PlatformDirectory`, `NetworkSection kind="outcomes"`, `FeatureTiles kind="artwork"`, `MediaSplitStack`, `RecognitionMarquee`, `ClientMosaic`, `ClosingCallToAction kind="primary"`, all inside one `SectionContainer max-width="site"` with `SectionGap hatch`.
- **worked well** — first screenshot is within ~60px of the 9414px reference and visually near-identical. `headerOffset="56px"` removed the extra hero height.
- **low** — `SiteNav` always shows "Login" on mobile; the reference hides it below xl. No prop for it.
- **low** — `HeroBand` prop docs say `carouselMarks` takes "registry names" but never list them; I used the names from `examples/hero/site-centered-carousel.vue`.

## 14:55 site-solution-web-apps — built
- `HeroWithOpening` (6 arguments, pi icons chosen by me), `MediaSplitStack` (4 bands, "Docs" buttons, illustrations `distributed-apis`, `retail-application-modernization`, `saas-platforms`), `TemplateGallery` (37 templates + stack ticker, registry names from `examples/template-gallery/site-default.vue`), `ClientQuotes`, `PlatformDirectory`, `NetworkSection kind="benefits"`, `RecognitionMarquee`, `FaqSection`, `ClosingCallToAction kind="split"` (with `titleMuted`). Screenshot ≈ reference (9782 vs 9833 px).
- **worked well** — the solution-page template maps 1:1 onto WebKit sections; `ClosingCallToAction split` with `titleMuted` reproduces "Build once. / Run everywhere." exactly.
- **high** — Font mismatch on every page: the shipped `@aziontech/theme@5.2.2` sets `--font-sans: Rubik`; webkit@5.12.0 depends on `@aziontech/theme ^4` (installed nested as 4.3.1) whose `--font-sans` is `Sora` — the face the reference uses. `src/webkit.css` (written by `init`) imports the app-level theme, so headings/body render in Rubik, narrower than the reference. Decision: keep the tarball the brief requires; not fixable without hand-overriding a token.
- **medium** — Page copy gave only the first ClientQuotes quote; the reference shows 6 client tabs (GFG, Axur, Zoop, HeroSpark, Contabilizei, GPA). I used WebKit's `examples/client-quotes/site-default.vue` quotes for Axur/Zoop/HeroSpark/Contabilizei and dropped GPA (no copy). 5 cells instead of 6.
- **medium** — FAQ: pages.json gives only questions (answers are collapsed in the reference). I wrote one-sentence answers from the page's own claims. `FaqSection` requires `answer`.
- **low** — pages.json structure is truncated mid-template list ("full tree in structure/…txt", a file that is not in the job folder); the rest of the page came from the screenshots. (Brief/data issue, not WebKit.)
- **low** — `@aziontech/icons` colour CSS header says icons are `ai-*-cor`; the real class is `ai-cor ai-<name>`. Template icons need mono glyphs (`ai ai-astro`), which exist only in the font, with no catalog in the webkit docs telling which framework glyphs exist (grep'd `azionicons.css`).

## 15:00 site-pricing — built
- `HeroBand kind="centered-band" title-length="long"`, `PricingPlans` (Monthly/Annual toggle; annual Pro price "$20" taken from the WebKit example — the reference copy only shows monthly), `FeatureTiles kind="illustrated"`, `ComparePlans` (9 product bands, ~90 rows), `PlatformDirectory`, `FaqSection` (12 questions), `ClosingCallToAction kind="primary"`. Screenshot ≈ reference (11592 vs 11726 px); comparison table identical row for row, mobile plan picker works.
- **blocker (for the build script)** — `ComparePlans` (`src/components/sections/compare-plans/compare-plans.vue`) fails `vue-tsc --noEmit`: `TS2304 Cannot find name 'section'` at lines 241–312 (the `v-for="(section, sectionIndex) in sections"` on `<tbody>` loses scope after the `<Overline>` child), and the failure cascades into the consuming SFC (my `ClosingCallToAction` bindings on the same page get bogus `Property 'value' does not exist`). Same with TS 5.9 and TS 6.0, with and without `htmlAttributes`. Webkit's own source cannot be type-checked by the consumer's `vue-tsc`. Decision: `build` = `vite build`; `typecheck` = `vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` kept as a separate script (it reports only these errors). ~15 min lost bisecting.
- **medium** — `ComparePlans` row values are one-per-plan; the pages.json tree de-duplicates equal cells, so I had to guess which plan a two-value row maps to (assumed Hobby = Pro, Enterprise differs). The table structure itself mapped 1:1 onto `sections[].rows[]` with `group: true` headers — **worked well**.
- **low** — `PricingPlans` "Popular" tag renders a filled orange chip; the reference is a soft tinted chip. No prop for the tag style.

- **medium** — `examples/hero-form/site-contact-split.vue` posts the form straight to a HubSpot endpoint with `fetch` from the page; the brief forbids runtime network calls, and `rules/webkit-sections.md` says "the section never posts … send from the site". Wrote a mock `@submit` that flips `loading` → `submitted` after 600 ms.
- **low** — `HeroFormField.kind` is a string union not exported in a way the docs mention; a plain array literal fails type-check (`string` not assignable to `HeroFormFieldKind`) until each `kind` is written `'text' as const`.
- **low** — `ClientQuotes` `mark` names are slugs of `CLIENTS[].name` in `src/assets/logos/clients/registry.ts` (`'global-fashion-group'`); documented nowhere — found by reading source.

## 15:08 Final checks

# DONE — job S1

## Pages
- `site-home`: built — all 9 bands (hero + client ticker, primitives directory, network/outcomes, Why Azion tiles, 5 use-case rows, recognition marquee, client mosaic, closing CTA). Missing: nothing structural; font differs (see problem 1); "Login" shows on mobile nav.
- `site-pricing`: built — hero, plan cards with Monthly/Annual toggle, value tiles, full feature comparison (9 bands), primitives, 12-question FAQ, closing CTA. Gaps: FAQ answers written by me (not in the source copy); 2-value comparison rows mapped by assumption; annual Pro price taken from the WebKit example.
- `site-contact`: built — hero form (mock submit, no network), client strip, support/contact hub, client quotes, recognition, closing CTA. Gap: client quote tabs have 5 of the reference's 6 clients (no copy for GPA).
- `site-solution-web-apps`: built — hero with 6 arguments, 4 use-case rows, template gallery (37 templates) + stack ticker, client quotes, primitives, network/benefits, recognition, 11-question FAQ, split closing CTA. Gaps: FAQ answers written by me; 5 of 6 quote tabs.

Routes: `/` index + `/<id>` per page, Vue Router history mode, dark only (`<html data-theme="dark">`).

## WebKit pieces used most
`SectionContainer` + `SectionGap` (every page), `SiteNav`, `SiteFooter`, `PlatformDirectory`, `RecognitionMarquee`, `ClosingCallToAction`, `HeroBand`, `ClientQuotes`, `FaqSection`, `NetworkSection`, `MediaSplitStack`, plus `HeroWithOpening`, `HeroForm`, `ContactHub`, `PricingPlans`, `ComparePlans`, `FeatureTiles`, `TemplateGallery`, `ClientMosaic`, `WebkitProvider`, `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*` logos and illustrations.

## Top 5 problems with WebKit (by impact)
1. **Theme/WebKit version mismatch changes the typeface everywhere** (high): the shipped `@aziontech/theme@5.2.2` sets `--font-sans: Rubik`; webkit@5.12.0 depends on theme `^4` (Sora, the reference face) and npm nests a second theme copy. `init`/`doctor`/`check` say nothing.
2. **`vue-tsc` cannot type-check WebKit's own source** (blocker for the default build script): `ComparePlans` fails with `TS2304 'section'` and poisons the consuming SFC; `vue-tsc -b` also fails to resolve some `.vue` subpath exports (`site-nav`, `site-footer`, `link`, `webkit-provider`) that `-p` resolves. Build had to become `vite build` + a separate `typecheck`.
3. **Examples don't run as pasted in a consumer app** (high): marketing examples use `/marketing-components/...` URLs that exist only in WebKit's docs app (real form: `import x from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/...'`, mapping only in `src/assets/site-assets.json`), and the contact example `fetch`es HubSpot from the page.
4. **API reference is incomplete** (medium): `llms/components/*.json` prop descriptions are empty; prop types (`SiteNavMenu`, `HeroBandAction`, `HeroFormFieldKind`…) are never defined; "registry names" for marks/illustrations/ticker are listed nowhere; the `.md` links to `.specs/*.json` on GitHub, which consumers are told not to use.
5. **`init` wiring breaks its own pre-commit gate** (medium): eslint config without `ignores` and no `.stylelintignore`, so lint runs over `dist/` after the first build (hundreds of errors from WebKit's compiled CSS); Vite's template comment fails `webkit/authoring-standards`; devDependencies pinned as `latest`, which `doctor` then warns about.

## Build
`npm run build` (= `vite build`) passes and produces `app/dist/`, which works as a static SPA (unknown paths fall back to `index.html`, checked with `vite preview`). `npx @aziontech/webkit check`: 0 errors. `npm run typecheck` still reports the `ComparePlans` errors from inside WebKit (problem 2).
